_comment: ARM 36 — the MASK EXTREME at scale, LV-4 half.  Identical to arm 35
(_ext305_gps_dual_20min_m30i30.json) except for ONE knob:
network.rx_cb_carry_step_gate : true      (LV-4)
De-mean stays OFF, so the loader forces LV-5 off (GnssConfigLoadNetwork.cpp:6630) and
LV-1 is off — this is the SPEC §17 item-1 posture, 'LV-4 alone, LV-5 machinery idle',
carried to the mask extreme at 303 stations.  Read arm 35's comment block for the
design, the a00-sigma circularity check, and what is and is not gradeable.
THE ONE NUMBER THIS PAIR EXISTS TO PRODUCE: median postfit phase rms (STA rows,
network_pf_keyed.csv) of arm 36 over arm 35, at identical observations.  The LV-4
data-side cost measured so far, always as a one-knob pair at fixed masks:
obs 15 / iono 25, 61 sta   0.00800 -> 0.01080   +35 %   (arm 34, this session)
obs 30 / iono 30, 303 sta  <arm 35> -> <arm 36>   ?
PREDICTION, STATED BEFORE THE RUN.  The cost is not a constant of the mechanism — it
nearly halved from obs 10 to obs 15.  The mechanism §19.3 proposes is that LV-4's full
admission delivers carry information the observations do not support; the information
that is least supported is the low-elevation code that sets the receiver DCBs.  If that
reading is right the cost should keep shrinking as the mask removes exactly that code,
so predict +10..25 % here, i.e. materially below arm 34's +35 %.  If instead it returns
to ~+64 %, or grows, the cost is NOT about low-elevation code and §19.3's mechanism is
wrong even though its measurement stands.
SECOND PREDICTION, on the level (DIAGNOSTIC, invariant #5).  LV-4's level offset has
tracked the obs mask monotonically so far (-28.4 TECU vs GIM at obs 10, -2.6 at obs 15,
i.e. +25.8 TECU for +5 deg of mask).  If that continued naively to obs 30 the field
would be absurdly high, so it must saturate or reverse somewhere.  Predict arm 36 lands
ABOVE arm 35 but by a small margin (a few TECU), because at obs 30 there is little
low-elevation code left for the admitted carry to lock in — the same starvation that
arm 35's comment predicts will hurt a00's observability hurts LV-4's actuator too.
READ THE a00 SIGMA FIRST.  If std_tecu approaches the 2.0 prior in EITHER arm, both
level numbers are prior-driven and neither prediction above can be scored.  The rms
grade survives that; the level read does not.
Fresh lineage, own paths; never resume onto another arm's snapshot.
NOTE ON THE EXTENDS LINE.  This arm extends _ext305_gps_dual_1h.json directly rather
than arm 35, and restates arm 35's overrides verbatim.  Chaining off arm 35 would sit
one level deeper than the loader's 8-level guard allows and the run dies at load
(measured: 'chain deeper than 8 levels ... refusing to continue').  Keeping both arms
at the SAME depth off the same base also makes the one-knob claim structural: the two
files differ by exactly rx_cb_carry_step_gate and the two output paths.
